messages.subject: ggplot 0.9, choropleth and legends
parts:
I'm still new to ggplot but have grown to love it in the past 6 months. Using sample code from from the "choropleth challenge" to help me come up with a solution, I was generating maps from live data to create a series of images for a "time lapse" display. However, when a local administrator loaded 0.9 recently, my process ended. I assumed it was only due to "pal" not being recognized in scale_fill_brewer but after correcting that, the legends and color assignments are refined to not include bins/breaks that are empty. I had 8 colors representing different categories and regardless of whether an area was in a given state, all the color assignments remained the same and the legend was full. Now if one of the bins is empty, it rescales the colors and I lose consistency between graphs.

From the example Hadley provided to the challenge a few years ago: https://gist.github.com/233134#file_polygons.r you can see what I'm experiencing after fixing the "pal" to "palette" and setting a group of unemployment rates to zero (like unemp$rate[unemp$rate <5 ] = 0 prior to the choropleth assignment).

I'm reading about the new geom_map and looking at revisiting the code but is there a simple way to get similar scaling from 0.8.9?
